home_description: Interactive volleyball rotations: see where to stand in every rotation for your position, drill the overlap rule, print lineup sheets and track matches. In English and Hungarian.
search_description: Search every page of the site.

system_51_desc: 5-1: one setter sets in all six rotations. Three front-row attackers when the setter is in the back row, two when they are in front.
system_62_desc: 6-2: two setters, and whichever is in the back row sets, so there are always three front-row attackers. The front-row setter attacks as an opposite.
system_42_desc: 4-2: two setters, and whichever is in the front row sets. Simpler to run, but only two front-row attackers.
system_66_desc: 6-6: no specialists, and nobody switches. Usually whoever is in zone 3 sets (some teams use zone 2). The usual way to start.
phase_receive_desc: The opponent is about to serve. At the serve hit your team must stand in rotational order.
phase_serve_desc: The player in zone 1 serves from behind the end line. Everyone else is in, or ready to switch to, their own spot.
phase_base_desc: The serve is over the net. Everyone has switched to their own spot and reads the opponent's pass.
phase_defense_desc: The opponent attacks. Blockers jump, everyone else digs or covers tips.
phase_attack_desc: The pass is up. The setter is at the target, hitters approach, and everyone else covers.
phase_transition_desc: You dug the ball: transition to attack. The setter runs to the target, hitters back off the net to approach.
task_serve_you: You serve. Afterwards, run straight to your defensive spot.
task_pass_you: You pass. The shaded area is yours: call the ball early and take everything that lands in it.
task_hide_you: You don't pass. Stand where the rules allow, out of the passers' way and their line of sight, ready for the next ball.
task_set_you: You set. Get to the target, just right of the middle at the net, and give your hitters a hittable ball.
task_block_you: You block. Close the gap to your teammate and take away the hitter's best shot.
task_dig_you: You dig. Stay low and still as the hitter swings; the shaded area is yours.
task_tip_you: You cover tips and roll shots behind the block. The shaded area is yours.
task_attack_you: You attack. Start your approach from here and time your jump to the set.
task_cover_you: You cover. Get low around your hitter to save a ball blocked back onto your side.
task_base_you: Stand in your base spot and read the opponent: who will they set?
libero_off_serving: Your middle ({middle}) is serving, and under FIVB rules the libero may not serve, so you wait off court. When your team loses the serve, you come back in for them.
middle_off: The libero is playing in your place in the back row (zone {zone}). You come back on when you rotate to the front row at zone 4.
tip_libero_rules: Libero swaps don't count as substitutions. They happen only while the ball is out of play, with at least one completed rally between two swaps, through the libero replacement zone: your bench sideline between the 3 m line and the end line.
tip_front_row: Front row: you may block, and attack from anywhere on your side. You may not block the opponent's serve, or attack it while it is in the front zone and entirely above the top of the net.
tip_back_row: Back row: you may not complete a block. To attack a ball that is entirely above the top of the net, take off from behind the attack line (3 m).
tip_libero_replaces: As libero you are playing in place of {middle}, the back-row middle.
tip_overlap: At the serve hit you must be {list}. Your feet count, not your body.
tip_setter_penetrate: Back-row setter: the moment the serve is hit, run to the target at the net. Don't leave early; that's an overlap fault.
tip_setter_front: Front-row setter: you may attack the second ball over the net (a dump), and you block on the right side like any front-row player.
tip_hide: Not passing doesn't mean resting: watch the server, then get ready to attack or cover.
tip_server: Serve within 8 seconds of the whistle, then run in to your spot at {slot}.
tip_middle_serves: Under FIVB rules the libero can't serve, so the middle serves and stays on until your team loses the serve.
tip_serving_overlap: Your league also holds the serving team to rotational order (the server excepted): {list}.
tip_switch: As soon as the serve is hit, switch to your spot at {slot}.
tip_serving_free: Under the 2025–2028 FIVB rules the serving team may stand anywhere on its own court, so you can already wait in your own spot. You are still a front- or back-row player by your rotation.
tip_base: Your spot is {slot}, whatever your rotation, until the ball is dead.
tip_pipe: Back-row outside: attack the 'pipe' in the middle, taking off from behind the 3 m line.
tip_back_attack: Back-row attacker: take off from behind the 3 m line. Landing in front of it is fine.
tip_66_setter: In 6-6 whoever is in zone 3 sets this rotation, so the setter changes every time you rotate.

overlap_description: Drag the six players around the court and see live whether the receiving team's formation breaks the overlap rule (FIVB rule 7.4), and why.
overlap_lead: This is the receiving team at the moment of the serve. Drag the players, or tab to one and use the arrow keys. The lines show the relations the referee checks: green is fine, red is an overlap fault.
overlap_court_label: Overlap trainer court, {rotation}. Each player can be moved.
overlap_keys: Keyboard: tab to a player, then use the arrow keys (hold Shift for bigger steps).
fault_depth: {back} must not be closer to the net than {front} (level is fine).
fault_side: {left} must not be further right than {right} (level is fine).
overlap_how_1: Each back-row player must be level with or behind the front-row player in front of them: 5 behind 4, 6 behind 3, 1 behind 2.
overlap_how_2: In each row, left to right: 4, 3, 2 in front and 5, 6, 1 behind.
overlap_how_3: Only these neighbours are compared. Zone 4 and zone 1 can stand anywhere relative to each other.
overlap_how_4: It is judged by your feet on the floor at the moment of the serve hit. Being level counts as legal, and afterwards everyone may move freely.

home_rule_title: New in 2025: the serving team may stand anywhere on its court
home_rule_text: Under the FIVB 2025–2028 rules, only the receiving team must be in rotational order at the serve. The right player must still serve, back-row players are still back-row players, and the serving team may not screen the serve or raise their hands above their heads until the ball has crossed the net. NCAA, US high school and USA Volleyball rules still check the serving team's order too, so the tools let you pick your league.
tip_libero_back: Libero: you may not serve, block or try to block, and you may never attack a ball that is entirely above the top of the net, from anywhere. If you set with your fingers from in front of the 3 m line, your hitter may not attack that ball while it is entirely above the net.
passers_fewer: In this rotation {n} players pass. The teammate the setter hides behind, or stacks with at the net, waits at the net with them instead of passing.
tip_no_switch: In this rotation many teams don't switch for the first attack after the pass: the outside, who passed on the right, attacks from the right, and the right-side hitter (the opposite, or in a 6-2 the front-row setter) from the left. Switching would send both across the court while the ball is in play. Teams differ; ask your coach. On defense and in transition you switch as usual.
tip_transition_simplified: Simplified: this shows the attack once the setter is at the target; blockers first back off the net to start their approach. Choose “The setter” under “First ball dug by” to see who sets when the setter digs.
where_metres: {net} m from the net, {left} m from the left sideline.
where_behind: Behind the end line, {x} m from the left sideline.
where_then: Then moves to {net} m from the net, {left} m from the left sideline.
quiz_revisit_note: Questions you get wrong come back more often until you get them right. Topics to review: {n}.
libero_off_serving_league: Your middle ({middle}) is serving. Your league lets the libero serve in only one position of the service order, and this is not the one your team chose, so you wait off court. When your team loses the serve, you come back in for them.
tip_middle_serves_league: Your league lets the libero serve in only one position of the service order, and this is not the one your team chose, so the middle serves and stays on until your team loses the serve.
tip_libero_back_league: Libero: your league lets you serve in one position of the service order. You may not block or try to block, and you may not attack a ball that is entirely above the top of the net. Check your rulebook for the other libero limits.
tip_libero_serves: Your league lets the libero serve in one position of the service order, and your team uses it here: you serve for {middle}. You may not serve in any other position this set.
league_help: Under FIVB rules since 2025 the serving team may stand anywhere on its own court, and the libero may not serve. NCAA, US high school and USA Volleyball still hold the serving team to rotational order, and let the libero serve in one position.
order_help: The player next after the setter in the service order. Most teams put an outside hitter there; some put a middle.
label_keep_sides: Outside who passed on the right
keep_sides_help: After serve receive, often in rotation 1, an outside who passed on the right can attack from there instead of running across the court, with the right-side player taking the left.
team_using: Using {team}'s playbook. Change it on the line-up page.
footer_accuracy: Spotted something wrong? We fix mistakes fast.
overlap_serving_free: Under FIVB rules the serving team may stand anywhere on its own court when the ball is served, so there is nothing to check: this shows your receive formation. Pick another league to practise the serving team's order.
overlap_serving_checked: Your league also checks the serving team's order. The server, behind the end line, is not compared with anyone.
playbook_help: How your team plays. The explorer, quiz and print sheets follow these choices when you pick this team.
playbook_receive_help: Drag players, or select one and use the arrow keys, to match where your team really stands. You can only save a legal formation. Rotations marked * use your own positions.
playbook_custom: This rotation uses your own positions.
playbook_suggested: This rotation uses the suggested positions.
share_help: The link holds the whole team, including names and numbers, in the address itself: nothing is uploaded. Anyone who opens it can add a copy to their own browser.
share_failed: Couldn't copy. Copy the link from the box instead.
import_found: Someone shared the team “{name}” with you.
match_league_limits: {subs} substitutions and {timeouts} time-outs per team per set.
match_sub_help_league: {used} of {max} used this set. Your league lets players re-enter more freely than FIVB rules do; this only counts substitutions against the limit, so check your league's re-entry rules. Libero swaps are not substitutions.
stats_help: Sideout: rallies won on the other team's serve. On serve: rallies won while your team serves. Low numbers show which rotation needs work.
stats_runs: Longest run of points in a set: {us} for you, {them} for them.
phase_cover_desc: The ball is set. The hitter attacks, and everyone else forms a cup around them to save a ball blocked straight back.
phase_defense_down_desc: The opponent can only send a down ball: hit standing or without a full swing. Blockers stay at the net without jumping, everyone else digs.
phase_defense_free_desc: The opponent can only send a free ball: an easy ball they could not attack. The setter goes to the target, and everyone else passes, front-row hitters dropping off the net.
task_stay_you: Stay at the net with your hands down: don't jump to block a ball hit without a jump. Be ready for a ball close to the net, then back off to approach.
tip_cover_pattern: This shows the usual teaching pattern: the three players nearest the hitter close in low, the other two cover deep. Teams vary the exact spots, so follow your coach's.
tip_cover_hitter: Swing hard: your teammates cover a ball blocked back. After the hit, get back to your base spot.
tip_free_front: Free ball: drop off the net to behind the 3 m line, pass if the ball comes to you, then approach.
tip_free_call: Call “free!” loudly as soon as you see the opponent can't attack, so everyone moves at once.
tip_down: Down ball: the hitter is standing, so the ball comes over flatter and slower than a spike. Blockers stay down; diggers stay low and deep.
tip_backup_libero: The setter dug the first ball, so you set. Set from behind the 3 m line, or with a forearm pass: under FIVB rules, a finger set by the libero from in front of the line may not be attacked while the ball is entirely above the net.
tip_backup_front: The setter dug the first ball, so you set this one instead of attacking.
tip_setter_dug: You dug the first ball, so someone else sets: the libero if on court, else the right-front player or another front-row player. Get up and be ready to cover.

tip_outside_shields: In this rotation you stay at the net and the setter hides behind you, so the opposite passes in your place.
tip_extra_passer: In this rotation you pass too, so the setter can hide behind a front-row player or the passing line stays full.
